subject: botany_2
question_text: Name any two artificially restructured plasmids.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.45, printed question 109. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Two names is the mark. The origin of each name is a cheap and memorable second half.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Two plasmids
steps.margin_note: Both names, spelled exactly. Three lines.
steps.why: Both were built in the laboratory from natural plasmids, which is what 'artificially restructured' means.
common_mistakes: Naming Ti plasmid. Ti is a NATURAL plasmid of Agrobacterium, not an artificial one.
Naming one plasmid. The question asks for two.
steps.memory_tip: pBR322 and pUC19: the two standard laboratory plasmids.

steps.label: What the names mean
steps.margin_note: Both origins, one line each. Six lines.

lines.text: Named after the people and the place that

lines: pBR322 is named after BOLIVAR and RODRIGUEZ,
who constructed it. The p stands for plasmid.
pUC19 is named after the UNIVERSITY OF
steps.why: Both names encode who made them, which is why they look arbitrary until the origin is known.
common_mistakes: Saying pBR stands for a property of the plasmid. It stands for the two makers' names.
Leaving out the second half. The origins are the easiest mark in the question.
steps.memory_tip: p for plasmid, then the initials of whoever built it.
